definition_zh: 醒来；唤醒；使觉醒；醒来；守灵；航迹
definition_en: to stop sleeping, or to make someone stop sleeping
core_image: 眼睛在暗里突然睁开，窗外刚从黑变蓝
scene: 凌晨四点，窗外一声闷响，他一下子睁开了眼。She woke at four and could not fall asleep again.
sceneCN: 这里 wake 是「醒来」（第 1 个义项：从睡眠中醒过来）；句意为她四点醒来，再也睡不着。暗里突然睁眼的那一刻，就是这个词的形象。

senses.title: To stop sleeping
senses.definition: to come out of sleep by oneself
senses.definitionCN: 自己从睡眠中醒过来
senses.example: She woke at four and could not fall asleep again.
senses.exampleCN: 她四点醒来，再也睡不着。
senses.why: Old English wacan meant to come out of sleep, and the word has kept that simple picture for a thousand years.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wacan 意为从睡中出来，这个词把这个简单的画面保留了一千年。

senses.title: To make someone stop sleeping
senses.definition: to rouse another person from sleep
senses.definitionCN: 把别人从睡眠中叫起来
senses.example: The noise of the lorry woke the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车的声音把整条街的人都吵醒了。
senses.why: English pairs wacan, to wake oneself, with weccan, to wake another; the two verbs merged into one.
senses.whyCN: 英语本有 wacan（自己醒）与 weccan（使别人醒）两个动词，后来合为一个。

senses.title: To become aware
senses.definition: to become conscious of something that was unnoticed
senses.definitionCN: 意识到原先未注意到的事
senses.example: The town woke to the danger only after the river rose.
senses.exampleCN: 直到河水上涨，全镇才意识到危险。
senses.why: Leaving sleep and coming to awareness are the same movement of the mind, so the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 离开睡眠与明白过来是心智的同一种动向，这个词于是两义兼具。

senses.title: A watch over the dead
senses.definition: a gathering beside a body before burial, or a vigil
senses.definitionCN: 下葬前守在遗体旁的相聚，或守夜
senses.example: Neighbours kept a wake in the old house all night.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们在那座老屋里守了一整夜灵。
senses.why: A wake was originally a night watch, and watching through the night gave the ceremony its name.
senses.whyCN: wake 原本是一次夜间守望，通夜守看的做法把名字给了这场仪式。

senses.title: The track left in water
senses.definition: the trail of disturbed water left behind a moving ship
senses.definitionCN: 船行进后在身后留下的水痕
senses.example: A small boat bobbed in the wake of the ferry.
senses.exampleCN: 小船在渡轮的尾波里上下摇晃。
senses.why: The track behind a ship shows where it has passed, and that visible track became the phrase in the wake of.
senses.whyCN: 船后的水痕标出它经过之处，这道看得见的痕迹便成了短语 in the wake of。

senses.title: A yearly village holiday
senses.definition: in the north of England, an annual local holiday once held at a church dedication
senses.definitionCN: 英格兰北部一年一度的村镇节日，原与教堂献堂日相连
senses.example: The whole village closes for the wake in August.
senses.exampleCN: 八月年节时整个村子都歇业。
senses.why: The night watch before a feast grew into the feast itself, so a village holiday still carries the name.
senses.whyCN: 节日前的守夜发展成了节日本身，于是村镇假日仍沿用这个名字。

intro.en: Wake is an Old English strong verb, and the noun for a night watch comes from the same root.
intro.cn: wake 是古英语的强变化动词，名词「守夜」同出这一词根。

items.en: Wacan meant to come out of sleep, and weccan meant to rouse another.
items.cn: wacan 意为从睡中出来，weccan 意为叫醒别人。

items.en: Related forms in other Germanic tongues all mean to be awake or to watch.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语中的相关形式都表示醒着或守夜。

items.en: In Middle English the two verbs merged, and woke replaced the older past form.
items.cn: 中古英语里两个动词合并，woke 取代了较早的过去式。

items.en: The noun for a night watch over the dead became the funeral wake.
items.cn: 表示夜间守候的名词发展为守灵仪式。

items.en: Sailors used wake for the water track behind a ship, and the phrase in the wake of followed.
items.cn: 水手用 wake 指船后水痕，短语 in the wake of 随之出现。

note.en: The first group holds the words built on the same root, the second the words for sleep and waking nearby.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词根上的词，第二组收周围与睡醒相关的词。

abstract.cn: 想房间还暗着，眼皮忽然睁开。

abstract.en: Hear a horn outside split the silence of the morning.

abstract.en: Picture a white trail widening behind a ferry.

definition_zh: 步行；散步；路程
definition_en: to move on foot, to go out for a walk, or a journey made on foot
core_image: 爷爷牵着狗沿河边慢慢走
scene: 爷爷牵着狗沿河边慢慢走Grandpa walks the dog slowly along the river.
sceneCN: 这里 walk 是「走路」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我每天走路去学校。

senses.title: To move on foot
senses.definition: To move on foot
senses.definitionCN: 用脚移动
senses.example: I walk to school every day.
senses.exampleCN: 我每天走路去学校。
senses.why: Old English wealcan meant to roll or turn, and the word came to mean moving on foot.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wealcan 意为滚动、转动，后指用脚行进。

senses.title: To go out for a walk
senses.definition: To go out for a walk
senses.definitionCN: 出门走一走
senses.example: We walked along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们沿着河边散步。
senses.why: The same motion, done for pleasure, becomes a walk in the park.
senses.whyCN: 同样的动作若为消遣而做，就成了公园里的散步。

senses.title: A journey made on foot
senses.definition: A journey made on foot
senses.definitionCN: 步行的距离
senses.example: It is a short walk to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 到车站走一小段路。
senses.why: The distance covered on foot gives the noun its sense of a route.
senses.whyCN: 步行走过的距离，使名词生出路程之义。

definition_zh: 战争；战事；斗争
definition_en: fighting between countries or groups with weapons over a long period
core_image: 地图上的两条战线，中间夹着一段没有人敢耕的地
scene: 旧相册里有一张黑白照片，几个年轻人站在泥里，背景是烧了一半的村子。The country was at war for more than ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 war 是「战争」（第 1 个义项：国家或群体之间长期持械交战）；句意为这个国家打了十多年仗。地图上两条战线的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Fighting between nations
senses.definition: organized armed fighting between countries or large groups, lasting over time
senses.definitionCN: 国家或大团体之间长期组织的持械交战
senses.example: The country was at war for more than ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家打了十多年仗。
senses.why: The word grew next to a Germanic form of the same base that also gave worse, and the meaning settled on armed conflict.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与同基底表示「更糟」的日耳曼语形式并行生长，词义最后落定在持械冲突上。

senses.title: A campaign against something
senses.definition: a determined effort to defeat a problem, such as disease or poverty
senses.definitionCN: 为克服疾病、贫困等问题而作的坚决努力
senses.example: The city began a war on rats in the old sewers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市开始了一场治理旧下水道鼠患的战争。
senses.why: Modern English extends the word to any long struggle that needs organized effort.
senses.whyCN: 现代英语把这个词扩展到任何需要组织起来的长期斗争。

senses.title: A struggle between ideas
senses.definition: in phrases such as a war of words, a fierce exchange of hostile speech
senses.definitionCN: 在 a war of words 等短语中指激烈的相互指责
senses.example: The debate turned into a war of words between the two professors.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论变成了两位教授之间的一场论战。
senses.why: Words that are exchanged like blows are described as a war, though nothing is broken.
senses.whyCN: 像拳脚一样来回抛的言语被叫作战争，尽管什么也没被打破。

senses.title: The state of being at war
senses.definition: the condition of opposing forces, as in war and peace
senses.definitionCN: 敌对力量相持的状态，如 war and peace 并用
senses.example: The novel opens in the year before the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说从战争前一年写起。
senses.why: English names the condition as well as the events, so one can live in the year before it.
senses.whyCN: 英语既命名事件也命名状态，所以人可以在它开始前的那一年里生活。

intro.en: War comes from Old Northern French werre, which spread from a Germanic word for confusion or disorder.
intro.cn: war 来自古北法语 werre，而后者源自日耳曼语表示混乱、纷扰的词。

items.en: A Germanic word for confusion or strife lies behind the French form, related to a form that gave worse.
items.cn: 法语词形背后是一个表示混乱、纷争的日耳曼语词，与给出 worse 的词形相关。

items.en: Old Northern French werre meant war, and Norman French brought it to England.
items.cn: 古北法语 werre 意为战争，诺曼法语把它带到英格兰。

items.en: English had its own word, werre, and the two forms settled into war.
items.cn: 英语本有 werre 一词，两种形式最后定形为 war。

items.en: The word was used of sieges and campaigns, and only later of wars between states.
items.cn: 这个词曾用于围城与战役，后来才专指国家之间的战争。

items.en: Modern English adds the war on disease and the war of words, both borrowed from bodily fighting.
items.cn: 现代英语又添出抗击疾病的战争与论战，都借自真实的打斗。

definition_zh: 警告；提醒；告诫；预先通知
definition_en: to tell someone about a possible danger or problem so that they can avoid it
core_image: 一个人伸手拦住同伴，指着前方，要他在踏出下一步之前先停下
scene: 山路边的牌子被风吹得咣咣响，护林员在岔口拦住游客。He warned us that the path would be icy after dark.
sceneCN: 这里 warn 是「警告、提醒」（第 1 个义项：告知可能发生的危险，以便对方避开）；句意为他提醒我们天黑后小路会结冰。伸手拦住同伴的动作，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：警告、告诫；提醒；预先通知

collocations.zh: 受到警告；要有心理准备

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「警告；警告信号」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「已受警告的」

加前缀 fore- 构成，义为「预先警告」

senses.title: To tell of danger
senses.definition: to tell someone about a danger or problem before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 在危险或问题发生之前告诉某人
senses.example: The coastguard warned the boats about the coming storm.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸警卫队警告船只将有暴风雨来袭。
senses.why: Old English warnian meant to take heed and to admonish; the word names the act of making someone careful before harm arrives.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 warnian 意为留心与告诫；这个词指在伤害到来之前使人警醒的动作。

senses.title: To advise against
senses.definition: to advise someone strongly not to do something
senses.definitionCN: 强烈劝告某人不要做某事
senses.example: Doctors warn against taking the pills on an empty stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 医生告诫不要空腹服用这些药片。
senses.why: The same forward look is aimed at an action: the danger is what the doing would bring, so the advice is a prohibition.
senses.whyCN: 同样是对未来的注视，只是这次落在某个动作上：危险正是这个动作会带来的，所以劝告成了禁令。

senses.title: To give notice in advance
senses.titleCN: 预先通知：提前告知某事会来
senses.definition: to inform someone in advance that something is going to happen
senses.definitionCN: 提前告知某人某事即将发生
senses.example: Nobody warned me that the office would close early.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人提前告诉我办公室会提前关门。
senses.why: With danger taken out, only the timing remains: the word still speaks of a thing before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 把危险抽掉之后，只剩下时间关系：这个词说的仍是事情发生之前的那一句话。

senses.title: To caution officially
senses.titleCN: 正式警告：由权威出面告诫
senses.definition: to caution a person officially, especially about behaviour or breaking a rule
senses.definitionCN: 由官方或权威出面告诫某人，尤指其行为或违规
senses.example: The referee warned the player before showing the card.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判在出示牌之前先警告了这名球员。
senses.why: An authority repeats the hedge at the cliff edge in a formal voice, and the next step is a penalty.
senses.whyCN: 权威以正式的口吻重演崖边那道拦阻，而下一步就是处罚。

senses.title: To keep someone off
senses.titleCN: 警告离开：阻止某人靠近
senses.definition: in the phrase warn off, to tell someone to stay away from a place or a person
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 warn off，令某人远离某地或某人
senses.example: The farmer warned the walkers off the closed field.
senses.exampleCN: 农场主警告散步的人离开那片封闭的田地。
senses.why: Here the warning becomes a wall of words: the message is not what to watch but where not to stand.
senses.whyCN: 此时警告变成了一道用话砌成的墙：信息不是该注意什么，而是不该站在哪里。

intro.en: Warn comes from an Old English word for refusing or forbidding, and it is close kin to 'beware'.
intro.cn: warn 来自古英语中表示「拒绝、禁止」的词，与 beware 关系很近。

items.en: Warnian meant 'to take heed, be careful', and also 'to admonish or forbid'.
items.cn: warnian 意为「留心、当心」，也表示「告诫、禁止」。

items.en: The noun waru meant 'care, protection, guard', part of the same Germanic cluster.
items.cn: 名词 waru 意为「注意、保护、看守」，属于同一日耳曼词群。

items.en: German warnen 'to warn' and Dutch waarschuwen in part share this history.
items.cn: 德语 warnen 与荷兰语的部分说法共享这段历史。

items.en: The shorter form warn came from the infinitive warnian, and the beware sense drifted to the separate word beware.
items.cn: 较短形式 warn 出自不定式 warnian，而「当心」这一义则漂移到独立词 beware 上。

items.en: The present range runs from a shout at a cliff edge to a formal letter from a court.
items.cn: 现代用法从崖边的呼喊一直到法庭的正式函件。

note.cn: 形近组收形状相近的 warn、war 类词；近义组收告知风险的多种说法。

definition_en: to use something carelessly so that it is lost, or material that is thrown away because it is no longer wanted
core_image: 水从没关紧的龙头里一直滴，地上积成一片没人要的湿痕
scene: 食堂收餐口的桶里堆着大半个没吃完的饭盒。So much food is wasted every day that the kitchen began weighing it.
sceneCN: 这里 waste 是「浪费」（第 4 个义项：不加珍惜地用掉，使之白白失去）；句意为每天浪费的食物太多，厨房开始称重。水白白流走、饭被倒掉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：废物、垃圾；浪费；荒地

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ful 构成，义为「浪费的；不节俭的」
加后缀 -age 构成，义为「损耗；浪费量」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「浪费者；废品」

senses.title: A desert or empty land
senses.titleCN: 荒地：无人居住的空旷之地
senses.definition: a large area of land that is empty, wild and not used for farming
senses.definitionCN: 大片空旷、野生、不用于耕种的土地
senses.example: Beyond the last field lies a wide waste of stone and thorn.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一块田之外，是一片石头与荆棘的荒地。
senses.why: Old French wast meant empty and desolate, and English kept that picture of land with nothing on it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 wast 意为「空的、荒凉的」，英语保留了那片空无一物的土地的画面。

senses.title: To destroy and leave empty
senses.titleCN: 使荒芜：毁坏而使之空无
senses.definition: to damage a place so badly that it is left empty or ruined
senses.definitionCN: 把某地毁坏到空无或残破的地步
senses.example: The long war wasted the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的战争让整个山谷变得荒芜。
senses.why: The adjective of emptiness becomes an action: to make a place into a waste.
senses.whyCN: 表示「空」的形容词变成动作：把某地变成一片荒地。

senses.title: Rubbish and unwanted material
senses.titleCN: 废物、垃圾：不再需要而被丢弃的东西
senses.definition: material that is no longer wanted and is thrown away
senses.definitionCN: 已不需要、被丢弃的物质
senses.example: The factory must treat its waste before it enters the river.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂必须先把废物处理掉，才能排入河中。
senses.why: What is left after use is like a wasteland: nothing grows on it, so it is set aside.
senses.whyCN: 用剩下的东西就像荒地：上面长不出什么，只好被弃置一旁。

senses.title: To use carelessly
senses.definition: to use money, time or effort badly, so that it brings no benefit
senses.definitionCN: 不善加利用金钱、时间或精力，使之无所收益
senses.example: Do not waste hot water on a small load of dishes.
senses.exampleCN: 别为几个碗浪费热水。
senses.why: Spending what could have been used well turns a resource into waste; the verb names that turning.
senses.whyCN: 把本可好好利用的东西花掉，资源就变成了废物；动词命名的正是这一转变。

senses.title: As in wasted effort or a wasted chance
senses.titleCN: 白白错过：努力或机会被耗掉
senses.definition: used of effort, opportunity or a person's condition when something valuable comes to nothing
senses.definitionCN: 用于努力、机会或人的状态，指宝贵的东西最终落空
senses.example: All their careful planning was wasted when the road was closed.
senses.exampleCN: 路一封闭，他们所有的精心安排都白费了。
senses.why: The lost value is no longer money but possibility: what might have happened now cannot.
senses.whyCN: 失去的不再是钱，而是可能性：本可能发生的事如今不可能了。

intro.en: Waste came from Latin vastus through Old French, and its first meaning was empty land.
intro.cn: waste 经古法语来自拉丁语 vastus，最初的意思是空旷的土地。

items.en: Vastus meant 'empty, desolate, huge'; the emptiness came before the size in English use.
items.cn: vastus 意为「空的、荒凉的、巨大的」；在英语用法中，空义先于大义。

items.en: The verb vastare meant 'to lay waste, to devastate', turning emptiness into an action.
items.cn: 动词 vastare 意为「使荒芜、毁坏」，把「空」变成了动作。

items.en: Old French had both gast and waste, meaning 'empty, ruined' and 'a waste place'.
items.cn: 古法语有 gast 与 waste 两种形式，意为「空的、毁坏的」与「荒地」。

items.en: English took waste as noun, adjective and verb together in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪同时把 waste 用作名词、形容词和动词。

items.en: Industry added the rubbish sense: household waste, waste paper, waste water.
items.cn: 工业补充了垃圾义：生活垃圾、废纸、废水。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same empty-root family; the near-meaning group gathers ways of squandering and of rubbish.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「空」词根词族；近义组收挥霍与垃圾类说法。

entries.definition: Extremely large; the same Latin vastus, with the size sense only.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「辽阔的」，同出拉丁语 vastus，只保留「大」义。

entries.definition: To destroy a place completely; Latin de- plus vastare.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「毁坏」，由 de- 加 vastare 构成。

entries.definition: Using more than is needed; the adjective of the squandering sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「浪费的」，是挥霍义的形容词形式。

entries.definition: Land that is empty and cannot be farmed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荒地」，即空旷无法耕种之地。

entries.definition: To spend money or time foolishly; stronger and more disapproving.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挥霍」，语气更强、更带责备。

entries.definition: Unwanted things; the British everyday word for waste.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾」，是英式日常说法。

entries.definition: Waste food and household rubbish; the American everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾」，尤指厨余，是美式日常说法。

entries.definition: To give or use without harming oneself; the opposite of wasting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「腾出、剩下」，与浪费相对。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 vastus，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: waste and vast share a root: empty land, and land just very big.
normal.cn: waste 与 vast 同根：一片是空地，一片只是很大。

normal.en: To waste is to turn a resource into rubbish.
normal.cn: waste 就是把资源变成垃圾。

normal.en: A waste of time costs more than a waste of paper.
normal.cn: 浪费时间的代价比浪费纸张大得多。

normal.en: Household waste is what leaves the house to be thrown away.
normal.cn: household waste 就是被运出家门的垃圾。

normal.en: Lay waste to a place and it becomes a waste: the verb and the noun meet.
normal.cn: lay waste to 一个地方，它就变成一片 waste：动词与名词在此相遇。

abstract.en: Picture a tap left dripping overnight: the water is not dirty, only lost.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水龙头一夜没关紧：水并不脏，只是白白流掉了。

abstract.en: The two halves of the word meet at the same point: what is thrown away is what was never used well.
abstract.cn: 这个词的两半在同一点相遇：被丢弃的，正是从未被好好利用的。

abstract.en: Emptiness is the hinge: a wasted field, a wasted chance and a waste bin all hold nothing useful.
abstract.cn: 空是那个铰链：荒掉的地、白费的机会、垃圾箱，都装着没用的东西。

examples.en: He wasted two hours waiting for a bus that never came.
examples.cn: 他白等了两个小时，那趟公交始终没来。

examples.en: The city collects household waste every Tuesday.
examples.cn: 这座城市每周二收集生活垃圾。

examples.en: It is a waste of money to buy a new one when this still works.
examples.cn: 这个还能用，再买个新的纯属浪费钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂（wei）死它（ste）」——把好东西喂给垃圾桶，活活浪费：浪费

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of waste start from empty land, move to the act of emptying a place, then to rubbish, to squandering, and finally to any chance that comes to nothing.
sensesIntro.cn: waste 的五个义项从荒地开始，到把地方弄空的动作，再到垃圾、挥霍，最后是一切落空的机会。

branches.en: LAND LINE: empty ground, and the act of making it empty.
branches.cn: 土地线：空旷的地，以及把它弄空的动作。

branches.en: RUBBISH LINE: what use leaves behind is thrown away.
branches.cn: 垃圾线：使用之后剩下的被丢弃。

branches.en: SQUANDER LINE: resources used so badly they become rubbish.
branches.cn: 挥霍线：资源被用得极糟，于是成了垃圾。

branches.en: CHANCE LINE: the lost thing is now possibility, not money.
branches.cn: 机会线：失去的已是可能性而非金钱。

branches.en: CONTRAST: spare keeps something; waste loses it.
branches.cn: 对照线：spare 留下东西，waste 让它失去。

definition_en: a ridge of water moving across a surface; also a hand gesture, a physical oscillation, and a surge of events or feeling
core_image: 海面上一道隆起的水脊向前推，到了岸边翻卷、散成白沫
scene: 退潮后的沙滩上，孩子追着一道涌上来的水脊跑，脚背被拍了一下，他说，A wave broke over my feet and pulled the sand from under them.
sceneCN: 这里 wave 指「水面向前推进的隆起水脊」（第 1 个义项：海上的波浪）；句意为：一道浪打过我的脚背，把脚下的沙也抽走了。

pos.zh: 波浪；波（物理）；挥手；浪潮；一阵（情绪）

senses.title: A ridge on the water
senses.definition: a raised ridge of water travelling across the surface of the sea or a lake, often breaking when it reaches shallow water
senses.definitionCN: 在海面或湖面上向前推进的隆起水脊，到浅水处常会翻卷破碎
senses.example: A wave broke over my feet and pulled the sand from under them.
senses.exampleCN: 一道浪打过我的脚背，把脚下的沙也抽走了。
senses.why: the noun came from Old English wǣg 'billow', the name of a moving ridge of water; this is the literal core that every other sense borrows from.
senses.whyCN: 名词出自古英语 wǣg「巨浪」，本义就是水中移动的脊；这是其余所有义项借用的字面核心。

senses.title: A sign with the hand
senses.definition: a movement of the hand held up and moved from side to side, used to greet, signal or say goodbye
senses.definitionCN: 举起手左右摆动，用来打招呼、示意或告别
senses.example: She gave a quick wave from the platform and disappeared into the train.
senses.exampleCN: 她在站台上匆匆挥了一下手，就消失在车厢里。
senses.why: the noun form of this sense grew from the verb: a single act of moving the hand to and fro was turned into a countable event.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项的名词形式是从动词长出来的：把一次来回动手的动作，变成了一个可数的事件。

senses.title: A physical oscillation
senses.definition: a disturbance that transfers energy through a medium or through space, repeating in time and distance
senses.definitionCN: 在介质或空间中传递能量的扰动，在时间与距离上重复出现
senses.example: Sound travels as a wave that compresses the air in front of it.
senses.exampleCN: 声音以波的形式传播，压缩前方的空气。
senses.why: physics took the water picture and generalised it: anything that repeats through space and time is drawn with the same rising and falling shape.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把水的图像一般化：任何在空间与时间上重复的东西，都用同一种起伏形状来画。

senses.title: A sudden surge of feeling
senses.definition: a sudden rise and passing of a feeling that affects a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 突然涌起又退去、影响一个人或一群人的情感
senses.example: A wave of relief passed through the ward when the doctor smiled.
senses.exampleCN: 医生一笑，一阵宽慰的波浪掠过病房。
senses.why: a feeling that comes in cycles and then passes behaves like water, so English counts emotions in waves rather than in units.
senses.whyCN: 情绪一波波涌来又退去，行为像水，因此英语用「波」来计数情感，而不是用单个单位。

senses.title: A wave of events
senses.definition: a cluster of similar events arriving close together, as in a crime wave or a wave of protests
senses.definitionCN: 同类事件集中在一段时间内接连发生，如犯罪浪潮或抗议浪潮
senses.example: The city reported a wave of bicycle thefts last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市去年春天报告了一波自行车失窃案。
senses.why: statistics describe clustered events as arriving in successive crests, so a rise in the count is drawn as a wave even when no water is involved.
senses.whyCN: 统计把集中发生的事件说成一个个接连而来的波峰，因此计数上升时，即便没有水，也画成一道浪。

senses.title: A curve in the hair
senses.definition: a curl or series of curves pressed or set into hair
senses.definitionCN: 在头发上做出的卷曲或一连串弧形
senses.example: A single wave in her hair softened the whole portrait.
senses.exampleCN: 她头发上的一道波浪让整幅肖像柔和下来。
senses.why: a lock of hair bent into alternating curves reproduces a water wave in miniature, so hairdressing kept the noun for the shape.
senses.whyCN: 一缕头发弯成交替的弧线，就是水波的缩小版，因此美发业保留了这个名词来指那种形状。

senses.title: A drawn line on an instrument
senses.definition: one rise and fall traced by a signal on a graph, screen or recording
senses.definitionCN: 信号在图表、屏幕或记录上画出的一次起伏
senses.example: The oscilloscope drew a clean wave across the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 示波器在屏幕上画出一道干净的波形。
senses.why: an instrument traces rising and falling voltage as a line, and the drawn shape is literally called a wave, so the graph keeps the sea's name.
senses.whyCN: 仪器把升降的电压画成一条线，画出的形状就被直接叫作波，图表于是沿用了海的名字。

senses.title: To move the hand
senses.definition: to move the hand or an object held in it to and fro, usually as a greeting or signal
senses.definitionCN: 把手或手中的东西来回挥动，通常表示招呼或示意
senses.example: He waved until the car turned the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 他一直挥手，直到汽车转过街角。
senses.why: the verb sense keeps the older gesture meaning, from Old English wafian 'to move to and fro', which is a different source from the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词义保留较古的手势义，出自古英语 wafian「来回挥动」，与名词的来源并不相同。

senses.title: To set into curves, or flutter
senses.definition: to give hair a wavy shape, or of a flag, cloth or branch, to move in curves in the wind
senses.definitionCN: 把头发做成波浪形；或指旗、布、枝条在风中起伏摆动
senses.example: Flags waved along the pier as the wind rose.
senses.exampleCN: 风起时，码头上的旗子一路飘动。
senses.why: the same verb extends from the hand to anything made to move in curves, from hair set in waves to cloth lifting in the wind.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词从手扩展到任何被弄成曲线运动的东西，从做成波浪的头发到风中掀起的布。

intro.en: Wave has two Old English sources: the noun wǣg 'billow' and the verb wafian 'to move to and fro'. They are generally treated as separate formations that came to share one spelling in Middle English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: wave 有两个古英语来源：名词 wǣg「巨浪」与动词 wafian「来回挥动」。学界一般把它们视为两个不同的构造，到中古英语才共用同一个拼写。年代均为约数。

items.en: Wǣg meant a moving ridge of water, 'billow, surge'; it is the noun that survives in modern wave and still names the sea's ridge.
items.cn: wǣg 指水中移动的脊，即「巨浪、涌浪」；它就是留存到现代 wave 的名词，仍指海上的水脊。

items.en: The Germanic noun is reconstructed as *wēgaz; it is generally connected with a root meaning 'to carry, move', though that link is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 其日耳曼名词重构为 *wēgaz；一般认为它与表示「运送、移动」的词根有关，但这一联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Wafian meant 'to move the hand or an object to and fro'; it is a separate verb, not a derivative of the noun wǣg.
items.cn: wafian 意为「把手或物件来回挥动」；它是一个独立的动词，并非名词 wǣg 的派生。

items.en: Both words came to be spelled wave, and the noun widened from a water ridge to a mass of advancing troops, events or feeling.
items.cn: 两个词都写成 wave，名词也从水脊扩展到推进的人群、事件或情感。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century physics began drawing waves on paper, and the vocabulary of wavelength, waveform and wave theory followed.
items.cn: 18 与 19 世纪的物理学开始在纸上画波，wavelength、waveform 与波理论等词汇随之出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (root relation, not first date): whether wǣg and wafian descend from a single root is disputed, and they are usually described as two formations that merged in spelling; the date of the first figurative wave of is approximate, and *wēgaz is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（指词根关系，不是首见年代）：wǣg 与 wafian 是否同出一根有争议，通常被描述为两个构造在拼写上合并；最早的比喻搭配（「一波……」这类说法）年代只是约数，*wēgaz 属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the derived forms of wave and one sound-alike with a different root; group two holds the sea words that differ in size, shape or behaviour.
note.cn: 第一组是 wave 的派生形式，以及一个词根不同的同音形近词；第二组是规模、形状或行为不同的海面用词。

entries.definition: from Old French weyver 'to abandon', probably of Scandinavian origin; it sounds identical to wave but means to give up a right, fee or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 weyver「放弃」，源头可能在斯堪的纳维亚语；它与 wave 同音，却意为放弃权利、费用或规则。

entries.definition: wave plus -y: having a shape that rises and falls in curves, used of hair, lines and edges.
entries.definitionCN: wave 加 -y：形状呈起伏的曲线，多用于头发、线条与边缘。

entries.definition: the distance between two successive crests; it is a measurement, not an object you can see on the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 相邻两个波峰之间的距离；它是一个量值，不是海上看得见的物体。

entries.definition: wave plus -let 'small': a small wave, and in modern signal analysis a short, localised wave shape.
entries.definitionCN: wave 加指小后缀 -let：小浪；在现代信号分析中指短而局部化的波形。

entries.definition: a long regular rise of the sea, often from distant weather, that has not yet steepened or broken.
entries.definitionCN: 海面上长而规则的起伏，常来自远处的天气，尚未变陡或破碎。

entries.definition: a very small wave on a surface, usually made by a light wind or a thrown stone.
entries.definitionCN: 水面极小的波，通常由微风或投石造成。

entries.definition: a wave that has begun to curl and fall as it reaches shallow water or a reef.
entries.definitionCN: 到达浅水或礁石时开始卷起、崩落的浪。

entries.definition: a great rolling mass of water, cloud or smoke; it stresses volume and movement rather than a single crest.
entries.definitionCN: 水、云或烟的一大团翻滚体；它强调体积与运动，而非单个波峰。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The noun is Old English wǣg 'billow'; the verb is wafian 'move the hand' — two sources, one spelling.
normal.cn: 名词是古英语 wǣg「巨浪」，动词是 wafian「挥动手」——两个来源，一个拼写。

normal.en: The family runs wave, wavy, waviness, wavelength, waveform, microwave, wavelet.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 wave、wavy、waviness、wavelength、waveform、microwave、wavelet。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physics: sound wave, shock wave, light wave, wave height.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：声波、冲击波、光波、波高。

normal.en: Figurative waves are counted: a wave of relief, a crime wave, a wave of protests.
normal.cn: 比喻的波可以计数：一阵宽慰、一波犯罪、一波抗议。

normal.en: One word covers hand and water because both go up and down and come back again.
normal.cn: 一个词同时覆盖手与水，因为两者都是上下往复。

abstract.en: Picture a single crest that keeps its shape while the water inside it stays almost in place.
abstract.cn: 想象一道波峰保持形状往前，而构成它的水几乎停在原处。

abstract.en: Picture a hand and a swell making the same arc in the air.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手与一道涌浪在空中画出同一条弧。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone drawing a line that rises and falls like water.
abstract.cn: 想象一支麦克风画出一条像水一样起伏的线。

examples.en: The buoy recorded a wave nearly twelve metres high.
examples.cn: 浮标记录到一道近十二米高的浪。

examples.en: She waved from the window until the bus was out of sight.
examples.cn: 她在窗前挥手，直到公交车看不见为止。

examples.en: A wave of new students filled the lecture hall in September.
examples.cn: 九月，一波新生坐满了讲堂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挥」——挥手是 wave，海浪一来一回也像在挥手 → 波浪、挥手、波动

root: 名词古英语 wǣg「浪、波涛」（日耳曼语重构 *wēgaz，一般认为是印欧「运送、移动」词根的派生）；动词古英语 wafian「来回挥动」；两源在中古英语合为 wave，现代义由水浪扩展到挥手、物理波与「浪潮」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses split between two old sources: the sea's ridge and its physical descendants, then the hand's gesture and everything else that moves to and fro in curves, with the counted surge of feeling and events in between.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项分属两个古老来源：先是由海浪扩展出的物理义，再是手势以及一切来回成曲线运动的东西，中间夹着可计数的情感与事件涌动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ridge of water moving forward while the water itself only rises and falls in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道水脊向前推进，而构成它的水只是原地上下起伏。

branches.en: THE DRAWN SHAPE: the sea's ridge and the oscilloscope's curve are one geometry seen twice.
branches.cn: 被画出的形状：海上的水脊与示波器上的曲线，是同一种几何看了两遍。

branches.en: THE HAND: the noun of greeting and the verb of greeting are the same gesture in two grammatical shapes.
branches.cn: 手：招呼的名词与动词，是同一个手势的两种语法形态。

branches.en: THE GENERALISED MOTION: physics extends the ridge to sound and light, and the verb to flags and hair.
branches.cn: 被推广的运动：物理学把水脊扩展到声与光，动词则扩展到旗与头发。

branches.en: SURGES COUNTED: feelings pass in crests, and social statistics cluster in waves.
branches.cn: 可计数的涌动：情感一波波过去，社会统计也一波波聚集。

branches.en: THE SHAPE IN HAIR: a curl repeats the water curve in miniature.
branches.cn: 头发里的形状：一道卷发把水的曲线缩小重演。

intro.en: Wave is a native Germanic word; its family grows by suffixes and compounds, and the same shape-word serves physics, hairdressing and signal analysis.
intro.cn: wave 是日耳曼本族词；它的词族靠后缀与复合扩展，同一个「形状词」同时服务物理学、美发与信号分析。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no cognate for wave: its word for a wave was unda, which gives English undulate but is unrelated to wave. That is why the Latin entries stay empty, and only the borrowed suffix -al appears elsewhere in the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有 wave 的同族词：它表示波浪的词是 unda，由此产生的英语词与 wave 并无亲缘。因此拉丁条目留空；词族里唯一的外来成分是别处出现的后缀 -al。

definition_zh: 我们
definition_en: the pronoun a speaker uses for a group that includes himself or herself
core_image: 几个人并肩站成一排
scene: 雨停了，孩子们从屋檐下跑出来，喊着我们可以回家了。The rain stopped, and the children ran out from under the eaves shouting we can go home now.
sceneCN: 这里 we 是「我们」（第 1 个义项：包括说话人在内的一群人）；句意：雨停后，孩子们从屋檐下跑出来，喊着我们可以回家了。

senses.title: The speaker together with others
senses.definition: the pronoun for a group that includes the speaker and at least one other person
senses.definitionCN: 指包括说话人和至少另一位在内的一群人
senses.example: We live in a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 我们住在一个小镇上。
senses.why: The speaker steps from the single self into a group, so the pronoun gathers several people behind one voice.
senses.whyCN: 说话人从单独的自我跨进群体，于是这个代词把几个人聚在同一个声音背后。

senses.title: People in general
senses.definition: used to mean people in general, especially when sharing a common situation
senses.definitionCN: 泛指人们，尤指共享某种处境时
senses.example: We should protect the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 我们应该保护地球。
senses.why: A group can widen until it means everyone who shares a problem, which gives the general sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体可以扩大到所有面临同一问题的人，于是生出泛指义。

senses.title: The author speaking for a group
senses.definition: used by a writer or speaker to refer to the work or group behind the words
senses.definitionCN: 作者或讲者用来指代文字背后的工作或团体
senses.example: As we showed above, the result is stable.
senses.exampleCN: 正如我们上文所示，结果是稳定的。
senses.why: A single writer speaks with the authority of a team, so we lends the sentence shared responsibility.
senses.whyCN: 单个作者借团队的分量说话，we 便给句子添上共同承担的分量。

intro.en: We is a native Germanic pronoun whose shape has barely changed in a thousand years.
intro.cn: we 是本土日耳曼语代词，一千年来形状几乎没变。

items.en: The ancestor form wiz already means we.
items.cn: 祖语形式 wiz 已经表示「我们」。

items.en: The word appears as we, with a long vowel.
items.cn: 古英语中写作 we，元音较长。

items.en: The spelling settles as we and the vowel shortens in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 中古英语中拼写定为 we，口语里元音变短。

items.en: We keeps its place as the plural subject pronoun.
items.cn: 近代早期，we 保持复数主格代词的位置。

items.en: We also serves as a general word for people sharing a situation.
items.cn: 现代英语中，we 也用来泛指处境相同的人们。

note.en: We changes case like I, and its meaning shifts between a real group and people in general.
note.cn: we 和 I 一样随格变化，词义也在真实群体与泛指之间移动。

definition_zh: 弱的；虚弱的；疲软的；差的；淡的
definition_en: not strong in body, force, effect or quality, and likely to give way under pressure
core_image: 一截被水泡软的细绳，拎起来时中间那段明显垮下去
scene: 雨下了整夜，屋檐下那根旧麻绳吸饱了水，挂上水桶后立刻往下坠。The old rope was weak after the rain and sagged under the bucket.
sceneCN: 这里 weak 是「弱的」（第 1 个义项：力量不足、容易垮掉）；句意为雨后旧绳变得不结实，挂上水桶就往下坠。那截被水泡软、中间垮下去的绳子就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 弱的；虚弱的；疲软的；差的；淡的

senses.title: Not strong in the body
senses.definition: having little physical strength, often because of illness or hunger
senses.definitionCN: 体力不足，常因疾病或饥饿所致
senses.example: After the fever he felt weak for several days.
senses.exampleCN: 退烧之后他虚弱了好几天。
senses.why: This is the bodily core: the muscles cannot do what they are asked to do.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体层面的核心：肌肉做不动被要求做的事。

senses.title: Likely to break or give way
senses.definition: easy to break, bend or damage under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下容易断裂、弯曲或损坏
senses.example: The rope was weak and snapped when the bucket filled.
senses.exampleCN: 绳子不结实，水桶装满就断了。
senses.why: The same lack of strength is then read into objects rather than bodies.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「力量不足」被从身体移到物体上。

senses.title: Low in force or intensity
senses.definition: small in force, loudness or brightness
senses.definitionCN: 力量、音量或亮度很小
senses.example: He answered in a weak voice from the back of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他在房间后面用微弱的声音回答。
senses.why: A light or a sound that carries little force is described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 散发不出多少力量的光或声音，也用同一个词形容。

senses.title: Not convincing or effective
senses.definition: not convincing, persuasive or effective in argument or action
senses.definitionCN: 在论证或行动中不足以让人信服或产生效果
senses.example: That is a weak argument and the committee will reject it.
senses.exampleCN: 那个论据很无力，委员会会驳回它。
senses.why: An argument that cannot stand up to a question is pictured as giving way under load.
senses.whyCN: 经不起追问的论据，被想象成在重压下退让。

senses.title: Poor in quality or ability
senses.definition: below the usual standard, especially in a subject or skill
senses.definitionCN: 低于一般水平，尤指某学科或技能
senses.example: I am weak in spelling, so I keep a list of hard words.
senses.exampleCN: 我拼写很差，所以留了一份难词表。
senses.why: Weakness in a skill is judged against a standard, not against a muscle.
senses.whyCN: 技能上的「弱」是相对标准而言，与肌肉无关。

senses.title: Diluted or lacking strength
senses.definition: containing too much water or too little of the active substance
senses.definitionCN: 水太多或有效成分太少
senses.example: This tea is too weak; let it stand a little longer.
senses.exampleCN: 这茶太淡了，再泡一会儿。
senses.why: A drink without enough substance is as weak as a body without strength.
senses.whyCN: 缺少实质的饮品，与缺少力量的躯体一样「弱」。

senses.title: Lacking firmness of will
senses.definition: not firm in will or judgement, and easily led
senses.definitionCN: 意志或判断不坚定，容易被带动
senses.example: They called him weak for agreeing so quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 他们说他这么快就答应，是太软弱了。
senses.why: Moral strength is imagined as a force too, so a person without it is weak.
senses.whyCN: 道德力量也被想象成一种力气，缺少它的人便「弱」。

intro.en: Weak comes from Old Norse veikr, a word for bending or giving way, which replaced an Old English cousin of the same meaning.
intro.cn: weak 来自古诺斯语 veikr，意为弯下、退让，它取代了同义的古英语亲族词。

items.en: The Germanic root meant to bend or to yield, and it stands behind words for pliancy as well as weakness.
items.cn: 这一日耳曼词根意为弯曲、让步，既支撑柔顺类词，也支撑软弱类词。

items.en: Veikr described anything that gives way under pressure and entered English during the Norse settlements.
items.cn: veikr 形容在压力下退让的事物，在诺斯人定居时期进入英语。

items.en: The loan drove out the native weak-related form and settled in spelling as weyk or weak.
items.cn: 这一借词排挤了本土形式，拼写定为 weyk 或 weak。

items.en: The adjective spread from bodies to ropes, voices, arguments and tea.
items.cn: 这个形容词从身体扩展到绳子、声音、论据和茶。

items.en: Weak tea and a weak point show how far the single image of giving way reaches.
items.cn: weak tea 与 weak point 显示了「退让」这一意象延伸得多远。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the shape of weak, the second gives the words that compete with it.
note.cn: 第一组与 weak 同根或形近，第二组是与之竞争的近义词。

normalIntro.cn: weak 始终表示力量不足，无论是身体、绳子、声音、论据还是一杯茶。

examples.en: She was still weak after the operation and slept most of the day.
examples.cn: 手术之后她仍然很虚弱，一天大部分时间都在睡。

examples.en: The bridge is old and weak, so heavy trucks are banned.
examples.cn: 这座桥又旧又不结实，因此禁止重型卡车通行。

examples.en: He is weak in grammar but very good at speaking.

branches.en: The intensity branch: a faint voice and thin tea.
branches.cn: 强度分支：微弱的声音与淡茶。

branches.en: The judgement branch: a weak argument and weak spelling.
branches.cn: 评判分支：无力的论据与很差的拼写。

branches.en: The will branch: too quick to agree.
branches.cn: 意志分支：答应得太快。

intro.cn: weak 是光杆形容词，词族由普通英语后缀 -ness、-en、-ly、-ling 构成。

latinIntro.cn: 这个词借自古诺斯语，并无拉丁来源，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 财富；大量钱财与资产；也指丰富、充裕
definition_en: a large amount of money, property and other valuable assets; also an abundance of something valuable
core_image: 一间库房堆着金条、地契与粮袋，角落里还立着一架书，物质与精神都显得充足
scene: 老人把一生的积蓄、房产与藏书都写进同一份清单。The family's wealth grew from land and trade rather than from wages.
sceneCN: 此处指「大量钱财与资产」（第 1 个义项：可估价的财富总量）；句意为这家人的财富来自土地与贸易，而非工资。图中可辨识物件：金条、地契、粮袋、书架。

pos.zh: 丰富；大量（用于表示「大量……」的固定结构）

forms.label: 复数（罕见，指多种财富形态）

senses.title: A large amount of money and assets
senses.definition: a great quantity of money, property, investments and other valuable things owned by a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体拥有的大量金钱、房产、投资及其他贵重物品
senses.example: Her wealth came from shares in the family firm.
senses.exampleCN: 她的财富来自家族企业的股份。
senses.why: The word names a large store of what people value, so its first sense is simply the quantity of money and goods held.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是人们所看重之物的大量积蓄，因此第一义就是所持金钱与物品的数量。

senses.title: Total net assets of a person or group
senses.titleCN: 个人或群体的净资产总额
senses.definition: the total value of assets minus debts, viewed as a stock at a point in time
senses.definitionCN: 资产总值减去负债，作为某一时点的存量看待
senses.example: The survey measures household wealth as assets minus mortgage debt.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把家庭财富算作资产减去房贷。
senses.why: Accounting turns a pile of possessions into a single net figure, which is the technical stock sense.
senses.whyCN: 会计把一堆财物变成一个净值数字，这就是技术性的存量义。

senses.title: Valuable natural resources
senses.definition: minerals, fertile land, water, forests and other natural endowments that a place possesses
senses.definitionCN: 一个地方拥有的矿产、沃土、水源、森林等自然禀赋
senses.example: The region's wealth lay in its forests and rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的财富在于森林与河流。
senses.why: A country can be rich without money in banks, because land and resources are also stores of value.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家可以没有银行存款仍然富足，因为土地与资源也是价值储备。

senses.title: Prosperity and wellbeing
senses.definition: the older sense of a good and flourishing condition, close to welfare rather than to money alone
senses.definitionCN: 较古的义项，指良好兴旺的处境，接近福祉而非单指金钱
senses.example: The old prayer asked for health and wealth for the household.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的祷词为全家祈求健康与兴旺。
senses.why: Before it meant money, the word meant a good state of life, and that older flourishing sense still colours religious and ceremonial use.
senses.whyCN: 在指金钱之前，这个词指良好的生活状态，这一较古的兴旺义仍影响宗教与仪式用语。

senses.title: An abundance of a thing
senses.definition: a large supply or great amount of something, as in a wealth of detail or experience
senses.definitionCN: 某物的大量供应，如大量细节或丰富经验
senses.example: The archive offers a wealth of detail about daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 这座档案馆提供了关于日常生活的丰富细节。
senses.why: Abundance of money and abundance of anything share the same shape, so the word extends to non-material plenty.
senses.whyCN: 钱财的充裕与任何东西的充裕形状相同，因此这个词扩展到非物质的丰富。

senses.title: The collective riches of a society
senses.definition: the total stock of valuable assets held by a whole society or economy
senses.definitionCN: 整个社会或经济所持有的有价值资产总量
senses.example: Economists study how wealth is distributed across the country.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家研究财富在全国如何分布。
senses.why: Once the word is applied to a whole society, it names an aggregate stock rather than one person's fortune.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦用于整个社会，命名的就是总存量，而非某个人的财产。

senses.title: Inherited or accumulated stock
senses.definition: riches passed down or built up over time rather than earned in a single transaction
senses.definitionCN: 经继承或长期积累而非一次交易所得的钱财
senses.example: Much of the family's wealth had been inherited from two generations back.
senses.exampleCN: 这家的财富很多是两代之前继承下来的。
senses.why: Wealth accumulates, so it often carries the idea of a stock built or handed down across time.
senses.whyCN: 财富会累积，因此常带有跨时间积累或传下的存量意味。

senses.title: The common good in older usage
senses.definition: the public good or general wellbeing of a community, preserved in the compound commonweal
senses.definitionCN: 共同体的公共利益或整体福祉，保留在「公共福祉」这一复合词中
senses.example: Old writers spoke of the wealth of the realm as its common good.
senses.exampleCN: 古代作者把国家的财富说成公共之善。
senses.why: The oldest sense tied riches to the health of a community, and traces of it survive in formal and historical language.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项把财富与共同体的健全相连，其痕迹仍留在正式与历史语体中。

intro.en: Wealth is native English, built from an Old English noun for wellbeing with an abstract suffix. It has no Latin ancestor and dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 财富是英语本族词，由古英语中表示安好的名词加抽象后缀构成。它没有拉丁语祖先，年代均为约数。

items.en: Wela meant 'wellbeing, prosperity, riches' and was related to the word for 'well'. It described a good condition before it described money.
items.cn: wela 意为「安好、兴旺、财富」，与表示「好」的词同源。它先描述良好处境，后描述钱财。

items.en: The abstract suffix -th turned wela into welth, the state of being well-off, in the Middle English period.
items.cn: 抽象后缀把 wela 变成 welth，即「富足的状态」，时在中古英语时期。

items.en: By the modern period the material sense of money and property dominated, while the older wellbeing sense survived mainly in compounds and religious language.
items.cn: 到近现代，金钱与财产的物质义占据主导，较古的安好义主要保存在复合词与宗教语言里。

items.en: The phrase a wealth of extended the word from money to any large supply, such as detail, experience or evidence.
items.cn: 「大量的」这一说法把词义从金钱扩展到任何大量供应，如细节、经验或证据。

items.en: Economics fixed wealth as a stock of assets held at a point in time, in contrast with income as a flow.
items.cn: 经济学把财富固定为某一时点的资产存量，与作为流量的收入相对。

items.en: Attestation uncertain (first citation of the material sense): the transition from wellbeing to money is gradual and no single first use is recorded.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定（物质义的）：从安好到金钱的转变是渐进的，没有单一的最早用例。

note.en: Group one separates near neighbours that are often mistaken for relatives; group two holds words for large possessions.
note.cn: 第一组区分常被误认作同族的近邻词；第二组是表示大量财物的词。

entries.definition: Health comes from Old English hælþ 'wholeness' and is related to whole, not to wela; the shared ending is deceptive.
entries.definitionCN: 健康来自古英语 hælþ「完整」，与「完整」一词同源，与财富的词根无关；相同的词尾容易误导。

entries.definition: Welfare joins 'well' with 'fare' meaning journey or condition; it is a separate compound, not a derivative of wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 福利由「好」与「行程、处境」合成，是另一个复合词，并非财富的派生词。

entries.definition: Commonwealth is common plus wealth, naming a political community that shares a common good; it is a relative but not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 联邦由「共同」加「财富」构成，指共享公共之善的政治共同体；它是同族词，却不是同义词。

entries.definition: Weal is the older noun for wellbeing from which wealth was built, and it survives mainly in set phrases.
entries.definitionCN: weal 是构成财富的较古名词，意为安好，主要保留在固定说法里。

entries.definition: Riches is a plural noun for abundant valuable possessions, often used figuratively for richness of experience.
entries.definitionCN: riches 是表示大量贵重财物的复数名词，也常比喻经验的丰富。

entries.definition: Fortune is a very large amount of money owned by one person or family, close to the personal sense of wealth.
entries.definitionCN: fortune 指个人或家庭拥有的大笔钱财，接近财富的个人义。

entries.definition: Assets are the items of value on a balance sheet, the accounting parts from which net wealth is calculated.
entries.definitionCN: 资产是资产负债表上有价值的项目，是计算净财富的会计组成部分。

entries.definition: Affluence stresses a high level of consumption and goods rather than the stock of assets itself.
entries.definitionCN: 富裕强调高水平的消费与商品，而不是资产存量本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real native root, real compounds and real accounting phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的本族词根、真实的复合词与真实的会计说法。

normal.en: The root meant wellbeing before it meant money, so the older sense still echoes in formal language.
normal.cn: 词根先指安好，后指钱财，因此较古的义项仍在正式语体中回响。

normal.en: The abstract ending turns an adjective of goodness into the state of being well-off.
normal.cn: 抽象后缀把表示「好」的形容词变成「富足的状态」。

normal.en: A wealth of detail and a wealth of money share the same shape: a large supply.
normal.cn: 大量细节与大量金钱形状相同：都是一种充裕的供应。

normal.en: Economics keeps wealth as a stock and income as a flow, and the two should not be swapped.
normal.cn: 经济学把财富当存量、收入当流量，两者不能互换。

normal.en: The older public-good sense survives in the compound for a political community.
normal.cn: 较古的公共之善义保留在指政治共同体的复合词里。

abstract.en: Picture a storehouse where gold, grain and books sit on the same shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一间库房，金条、粮食与书摆在同一层架上。

abstract.en: Picture a river that keeps flowing while a reservoir holds its water still.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河不断流动，而水库把水静静存住。

abstract.en: Picture a society whose common good is written on a shared ledger.
abstract.cn: 想象一个社会，把公共之善记在一本共同的账上。

examples.en: The country's wealth is concentrated in a few coastal cities.
examples.cn: 这个国家的财富集中在少数沿海城市。

examples.en: She brought a wealth of experience to the negotiation.
examples.cn: 她为谈判带来了丰富的经验。

examples.en: Wealth can grow while wages stay flat, which widens the gap between owners and workers.
examples.cn: 财富可以在工资停滞时增长，从而扩大所有者与劳动者之间的差距。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「围」加「思」——把金条、地契与粮食围起来反复思量，就是财富；联想「围起来的家底」

root: 古英语 wela「安好、兴旺、财富」加抽象后缀构成，属日耳曼语本族词，没有拉丁语来源；其较古义为良好处境，后收窄为钱财与资产，并保留「大量、丰富」的引申义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one store of value: money and assets are added into a net stock, extended to land, to prosperity, to any abundance, to a society's total and finally to the common good.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一份价值储存展开：钱财与资产先被加成净值，再扩展到土地、兴旺、任何充裕、社会总量，最后到公共之善。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a storehouse holding gold, deeds, grain and books on the same shelves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间库房，金条、地契、粮袋与书都摆在同一层架上。

branches.en: THE STORE: possessions are first counted, then reduced to a net stock.
branches.cn: 储存：财物先被清点，再折算成净存量。

branches.en: THE LAND: value also lies in rivers, forests and minerals.
branches.cn: 土地：价值也藏在河流、森林与矿藏里。

branches.en: THE GOOD STATE: the oldest sense is flourishing life, not coin.
branches.cn: 良好状态：最古老的义项是兴旺的生活，而不是钱币。

branches.en: ABUNDANCE AND AGGREGATE: any large supply, and the whole society's total, share the same shape.
branches.cn: 充裕与总量：任何大量供应与整个社会的总量，形状相同。

branches.en: TIME AND THE COMMON: what is handed down, and what is held in common.
branches.cn: 时间与公共：一边是传下的存量，一边是共同持有的福祉。

intro.en: Wealth and its relatives are native English; no Latin source is involved, so the family is read from Old English alone.
intro.cn: 财富及其同族词是英语本族词，不涉及拉丁语来源，因此这个词族只能从古英语读起。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries for this word: the root is Germanic and the suffixes are native or French-influenced.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语条目：词根是日耳曼语，后缀为本族或受法语影响的形式。

items.example: Wealth accumulated over three generations.
The wealthy district built its own school.
items.exampleCN: 这个富裕城区自建了一所学校。

items.example: The coast grew wealthier than the interior.
The wealthiest families owned most of the land.
items.exampleCN: 最富有的家族拥有大部分土地。

items.example: Wealthiness brought political influence.
Old texts wished the town weal.
The commonweal was invoked in the debate.
items.exampleCN: 辩论中援引了公共福祉。

items.example: The scheme worked well for small farms.
items.exampleCN: 这项计划对小农场很有效。

definition_zh: 穿、戴；磨损、穿旧；耐穿；名词：磨损；衣着
definition_en: to have clothes on the body, to damage something by long use, or the damage caused by use
core_image: 一件外套的袖口被日日挽起，布料薄了、起了毛
scene: 冬天的早晨，她在门口匆匆披上大衣，围巾绕了两圈。He wore the same grey coat all winter and never complained.
sceneCN: 这里 wear 是「穿、戴」（第 1 个义项：把衣物穿在身上）；句意为他整个冬天都穿同一件灰大衣，从不抱怨。被日日穿戴而磨损的袖口，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：穿、戴；磨损、用旧；耐用
名词：磨损；衣着（多用于复合词）

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「磨破的；疲惫的」
加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「令人疲惫的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「穿戴者」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可穿戴的（含电子设备）」

senses.title: To have clothes on
senses.titleCN: 穿、戴：把衣物首饰带在身上
senses.definition: to have clothes, shoes, glasses or jewellery on the body
senses.definitionCN: 把衣服、鞋、眼镜或首饰带在身上
senses.example: She wears glasses only when she reads.
senses.exampleCN: 她只在看书时戴眼镜。
senses.why: Old English werian meant to have on the body; the idea is carrying something on yourself, not putting it away.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 werian 意为「穿在身上」；这一观念是把东西带在身上，而不是收起来。

senses.title: To have a look or expression
senses.titleCN: 面带：带着某种神情或气色
senses.definition: to have a particular expression or appearance on the face
senses.definitionCN: 脸上带着某种表情或样子
senses.example: He wore a tired smile all through the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 整场会议他都带着疲惫的笑。
senses.why: The face is treated like clothing: an expression can be put on and carried about.
senses.whyCN: 脸被当作衣物来对待：表情也能穿上身，带着走来走去。

senses.title: To damage by use
senses.titleCN: 磨损：长期使用而变薄变坏
senses.definition: to damage or make thin by long or repeated use
senses.definitionCN: 因长期或反复使用而磨损、变薄
senses.example: The stairs were worn hollow in the middle.
senses.exampleCN: 那段楼梯中间被踏得凹了下去。
senses.why: Use rubs away material; the same verb now describes what the wearing does to the thing.
senses.whyCN: 使用会磨去材质；同一个动词此时描述这种穿戴对东西做了什么。

senses.title: To last in use
senses.definition: to remain in good condition after much use, used of materials and products
senses.definitionCN: 指材料与产品经久使用仍完好
senses.example: Good leather shoes wear well for years.
senses.exampleCN: 好皮鞋能穿好多年。
senses.why: The same process is viewed from the object's side: either it rubs away or it holds.
senses.whyCN: 同一过程从物体这一侧看：它或磨掉，或撑住。

senses.title: The damage itself
senses.definition: the damage or loss of material caused by use
senses.definitionCN: 因使用造成的材质损耗
senses.example: Check the tyres for wear before the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途驾驶前检查轮胎的磨损。
senses.why: The action becomes a noun, and the noun names the mark left behind.
senses.whyCN: 动作化为名词，而名词指留下的痕迹。

intro.en: Wear is an Old English verb meaning to carry on the body, and it has always had both the clothing and the rubbing sense.
intro.cn: wear 是古英语动词，意为「在身上带着」，一直兼具穿戴与摩擦两个意思。

items.en: Werian meant 'to wear, to have on the body', and also 'to defend' in an older layer.
items.cn: werian 意为「穿、把……带在身上」，更早一层还有「防护」之义。

items.en: The past forms wore and worn keep an old vowel pattern shared with bear and swear.
items.cn: 过去式 wore 与过去分词 worn 保留了与 bear、swear 共有的古老元音模式。

items.en: A separate verb, often written werian as well, meant to weary or tire, and the 'wear out' sense grew partly from it.
items.cn: 另一个动词（也常写作 werian）意为使疲乏，wear out 的「耗尽」义部分源自它。

items.en: The clothing and the rubbing senses were already side by side, as they are today.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，穿戴义与磨损义已经并列，一如今天。

items.en: New compounds keep arriving: footwear, sportswear, wearable devices.
items.cn: 新的复合词不断出现：footwear、sportswear、wearable devices。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the wear family; the near-meaning group gathers dressing and damaging words.
note.cn: 形近组收 wear 一族词；近义组收穿衣与磨损类词。

entries.definition: Damaged by use, or very tired; the past participle as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「磨破的、疲惫的」，是过去分词转来的形容词。

entries.definition: Tiring to do or to be with.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人疲惫的」。

entries.definition: The person who has something on.
The question word for place; a homophone trap.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在哪里」，与 wear 同音，易混。

entries.definition: To put clothes on; more about the act than about having them on.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「穿衣」，侧重穿衣动作。

entries.definition: To place clothes on the body at one moment; wear is the resulting state.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「穿上」，指某一刻的动作，而 wear 是穿着的状态。

entries.definition: To wear away slowly by natural forces such as water or wind.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「侵蚀」，多指自然力缓慢磨去。

entries.definition: Of cloth, to become worn into loose threads.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「磨散」，多指布料磨出线头。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English werian and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 werian，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Put on is the moment; wear is the day that follows.
normal.cn: put on 是那一刻；wear 是之后的一整天。

normal.en: Wear out means both used up and tired out.
normal.cn: wear out 既指磨坏，也指累垮。

normal.en: Wear off is for a feeling or a mark slowly leaving.
normal.cn: wear off 指感觉或痕迹慢慢消失。

normal.en: When patience wears thin, the same cloth image is at work.
normal.cn: 耐心 wearable thin 时，用的还是同一块布的形象。

normal.en: Wore and worn follow the pattern of bore, borne and tore, torn.
normal.cn: wore 与 worn 遵循 bore、borne、tore、torn 的模式。

abstract.en: Picture a coat cuff rolled up every morning: the cloth thins exactly where the habit happens.
abstract.cn: 想象每天早晨都挽起的袖口：布料正是在习惯发生的地方变薄。

abstract.en: Clothing and erosion are one word because both are things carried and rubbed by daily life.
abstract.cn: 穿衣与磨损是同一个词，因为两者都是被日常生活带着、磨着的东西。

abstract.en: A face can wear a smile for the same reason a body wears a coat: both are put on for others to see.
abstract.cn: 脸可以带着笑，正如身体穿着外套：两样都是穿给旁人看的。

examples.en: He wore a dark suit to the interview.
examples.cn: 他穿了深色西装去面试。

examples.en: The carpet has worn thin near the door.
examples.cn: 门口那块地毯已经磨薄了。

examples.en: This jacket has worn well for six winters.
examples.cn: 这件夹克已经穿了六个冬天，依然耐穿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂（wea）儿（r）」——每天喂孩子穿衣，衣服慢慢被穿旧：穿；磨损

root: 古英语 werian「穿、带在身上」，源自日耳曼语同一词根；过去式 wore、过去分词 worn 保留古老元音变换；同族词有 worn、wearer、wearable。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of wear run from clothes on the body, to a look worn on the face, to material rubbed away, to a thing that lasts, and finally to the damage itself.
sensesIntro.cn: wear 的五个义项从身上的衣物，到脸上的神情，到被磨去的材质，到经得起使用，最后是磨损本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat cuff rolled up each morning, the cloth gone thin where the habit falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：每天早晨挽起的袖口，习惯落处布料变薄。

branches.en: BODY LINE: clothes and expressions are both carried on us.
branches.cn: 身体线：衣物与神情都是带在身上的。

branches.en: EROSION LINE: use rubs the material away.
branches.cn: 侵蚀线：使用把材质磨去。

branches.en: DURABILITY LINE: the same rubbing seen from the object's side.
branches.cn: 耐用线：同一摩擦从物体一侧来看。

branches.en: RESULT LINE: the noun names the mark left by use.
branches.cn: 结果线：名词指使用留下的痕迹。

branches.en: CONTRAST: put on is a moment, wear is a state.
branches.cn: 对照线：put on 是瞬间，wear 是状态。

intro.en: Wear is a strong native verb; its derivatives use plain English endings.
intro.cn: wear 是本族的强变化动词，其派生词使用普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

It forms wearer.
It forms wearing.

definition_zh: 天气；恶劣天气；经受住、渡过（难关）；使受日晒雨淋而风化；上风的
definition_en: the state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, or to come through a difficult period safely
core_image: 山顶的风把旗子吹得笔直，云从西边一层层压过来
scene: 山顶气象站外，风向标转得飞快，值班员把领子竖起来才敢推门。 A front is moving in, and the weather on the ridge turns foul by noon.
sceneCN: 这里 weather 指「某时某地的天气状况」（第 1 个义项：大气在特定时间地点的状态）；句意为一道锋面正在移来，中午前山脊上的天气就会变坏。图中可辨识物件：风向标、翻卷的云、百叶箱、被风压弯的草。

pos.zh: 天气；恶劣天气；（航海）上风的一侧
经受住、渡过；使受日晒雨淋而风化；使露天放置陈化
上风的、迎风的（航海用语）

forms.label: 名词复数（多种天气类型，少用）

senses.title: Atmospheric state
senses.definition: the condition of the atmosphere at a given place and time, described in terms of heat, cloud, wind and rain
senses.definitionCN: 特定地点与时间的大气状况，以冷热、云量、风与雨来描述
senses.example: The weather on the coast changes faster than any forecast can follow.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸的天气变化之快，任何预报都跟不上。
senses.why: the noun is uncountable here because it names a continuous state rather than one countable event.
senses.whyCN: 此处名词不可数，因为它指一种持续状态，而非一次可计数的事件。

senses.title: Rough weather
senses.definition: stormy or otherwise severe conditions that threaten travel, crops or safety
senses.definitionCN: 威胁出行、作物或安全的暴烈天气
senses.example: Fishing boats stayed in harbour through three days of weather.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船在恶劣天气里躲进港内三天。
senses.why: English often uses the bare noun where other languages need an adjective: the weather turned means it turned bad.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用光秃秃的名词表达贬义，天气变了就等于天气变坏了。

senses.title: Come through safely
senses.definition: to survive a storm, a crisis or a period of difficulty without being destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 在风暴、危机或困难时期中幸存而不被摧毁
senses.example: The small bank weathered the panic better than its rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小银行比对手更好地挺过了那场恐慌。
senses.why: the nautical image is of a ship that stays afloat through rough seas; the verb keeps that sense of enduring rather than avoiding.
senses.whyCN: 航海意象是一艘船在狂浪中仍浮着；动词保留的是「承受而非避开」的意思。

senses.title: Wear away by exposure
senses.titleCN: 因日晒雨淋而风化、变色
senses.definition: to become worn, faded or cracked through long exposure to sun, rain and frost
senses.definitionCN: 长期暴露于日晒、雨淋与霜冻而磨损、褪色或开裂
senses.example: The unpainted shutters had weathered to a pale grey.
senses.exampleCN: 没上漆的百叶窗已被风雨磨成浅灰色。
senses.why: this is the intransitive twin of the geological noun: the object does the changing itself, without any agent acting on it.
senses.whyCN: 这是地质名词的不及物孪生用法：物件自行改变，并无外力直接施为。

senses.title: Season timber in the open
senses.titleCN: 把木材露天放置使其陈化
senses.definition: to leave timber or stone exposed to the air so that it dries and stabilises before use
senses.definitionCN: 把木材或石料露天放置，使其在使用前干燥稳定
senses.example: They weather the oak boards for two years before planing them.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把橡木板露天放两年，再刨平使用。
senses.why: the same exposure that damages rock is deliberately used here to prevent later warping, so the sense is technical rather than negative.
senses.whyCN: 使岩石受损的同一种暴露，此处被有意用来防止日后变形，因此这一义偏技术而非贬义。

senses.title: Windward side
senses.definition: the side of a ship or ridge from which the wind blows, or the adjective describing that side
senses.definitionCN: 船或山脊迎风的一侧，或形容该侧的形容词
senses.example: Keep to the weather side of the buoy as you round it.
senses.exampleCN: 绕过浮标时，要保持在它的上风侧。
senses.why: sailors needed a word for the side that takes the wind first, and the noun already meant storm, so the sense came free.
senses.whyCN: 水手需要一个词指最先受风的一侧，而名词本已含风暴义，这一用法便自然生出。

senses.title: Under the weather
senses.definition: feeling slightly ill or out of sorts, without naming a specific disease
senses.definitionCN: 略感不适、精神不振，而不特指某种疾病
senses.example: She stayed home because she was a little under the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得有点不舒服，就留在家里了。
senses.why: the idiom comes from sailors sent below when seasick; being under the weather meant being under the deck in bad conditions.
senses.whyCN: 这个习语来自晕船的水手被送到舱下：在不佳的天气里待在甲板之下。

senses.title: Survive a public storm
senses.definition: to keep a reputation or an institution intact through public criticism or scandal
senses.definitionCN: 在公众批评或丑闻中保持声誉或机构完整
senses.example: The university weathered the scandal without losing its accreditation.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学熬过了丑闻，没有失去认证资格。
senses.why: the metaphor transfers rough seas to public opinion: the vessel is a reputation, and staying afloat is staying credible.
senses.whyCN: 比喻把狂浪移到舆论上：船成了声誉，不沉就是仍可信。

intro.en: Weather descends from Old English weder 'air, sky, storm', a word shared across the Germanic languages. Its deeper pre-Germanic source is unknown. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: weather 源自古英语 weder「空气、天空、风暴」，为日耳曼诸语共有。其在日耳曼语之前的更早来源不明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Weder named the sky and whatever came out of it, including storms; the modern restriction to atmospheric conditions came later.
items.cn: weder 指天空以及从天而降的一切，包括风暴；后来才收窄为大气状况。

items.en: From the fifteenth century the verb meant to expose something to the open air, and by extension to endure such exposure.
items.cn: 自十五世纪起，动词指让某物暴露于露天，并引申为承受这种暴露。

items.en: Sailors used the noun for the windward side and the verb for coming through a gale, and both senses entered general English.
items.cn: 水手用名词指上风侧，用动词指闯过狂风，这两个义项都进入了通用英语。

items.en: The phrase under the weather, recorded in the nineteenth century, referred to sailors sent below decks when seasick.
items.cn: under the weather 这一短语见于十九世纪，指晕船的水手被送到甲板之下。

items.en: Geology took the same verb for rock decay, giving weathering, where the exposure itself is the agent.
items.cn: 地质学用同一个动词指岩石分解，由此产生 weathering，其中暴露本身即是营力。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic ancestry of weder is unsettled, and any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：weder 在日耳曼语之前的谱系无定论，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates weather from look-alikes that share its spelling pattern but not its history; group two separates it from words about climate, storms and exposure.
note.cn: 第一组把 weather 与拼写相近却不同源的词分开；第二组区分它与气候、风暴、暴露相关的近义词。

entries.definition: A conjunction from Old English hwæther 'which of two', built on the interrogative stem; it is homophonous with weather but unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 源自古英语 hwæther「两者中哪一个」的连词，建立在疑问词干上；与 weather 同音但无亲缘关系。

entries.definition: From Old English wiþerian 'to shrivel'; the shared -ther ending is coincidence, since wither has nothing to do with sky or storm.
entries.definitionCN: 源自古英语 wiþerian「枯萎」；共有的 -ther 结尾只是巧合，wither 与天空或风暴无关。

entries.definition: Weather plus -ly: able to sail close to the wind, a technical cousin rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: weather 加 -ly：能抢风航行，是同族的技术用语，而非同义词。

entries.definition: The participle used adjectivally for surfaces worn by exposure; it describes the result, not the atmospheric state.
entries.definitionCN: 分词作形容词，指因暴露而磨损的表面；它描写结果，不指大气状态。

entries.definition: The usual pattern of weather over many years; weather is what you get today, climate is what you expect.
entries.definitionCN: 多年天气的常规格局：weather 是今天遇到的，climate 是预期中的。

entries.definition: A single violent disturbance with strong wind and rain; it is one kind of bad weather, not the general state.
entries.definitionCN: 一次伴有强风与暴雨的剧烈扰动，是恶劣天气中的一种，而非一般状态。

entries.definition: A neutral plural used in reports for the state of the atmosphere, often when numbers follow.
entries.definitionCN: 报告中用于指大气状态的中性复数，常在后接数据时使用。

entries.definition: Being left open to the elements; it names the cause that weather, as a verb, sets in motion.
entries.definitionCN: 被置于露天之中；它指 weather 作动词时所启动的那个原因。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The noun is uncountable: one says fine weather, not a fine weather.
normal.cn: 名词不可数：应说好天气，而不说一个好天气。

normal.en: The verb keeps the nautical sense of enduring: weather the storm, weather the recession.
normal.cn: 动词保留航海的「承受」义：渡过风暴、挺过衰退。

normal.en: The family runs weathering, weathered, weatherly, weatherproof, weatherman.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 weathering、weathered、weatherly、weatherproof、weatherman。

normal.en: The idiom under the weather is about being seasick below decks, not about rain.
normal.cn: 习语 under the weather 指在舱下晕船，与下雨无关。

normal.en: Do not confuse the homophone whether, which introduces alternatives.
normal.cn: 勿与同音词 whether 混淆，后者引出两种选择。

abstract.en: Picture a flag nailed to a mast, taking whatever the sky sends.
abstract.cn: 想象一面钉在桅杆上的旗，天空给什么它就受什么。

abstract.en: Picture a ship that stays upright not by hiding but by riding each wave.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船不靠躲避、而靠随浪起伏而保持直立。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden bench outdoors, silvered by years of sun and rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一张户外木凳，被多年日晒雨淋漂成银灰色。

examples.en: The weather closed in and the ferry stopped running.
examples.cn: 天气变坏，渡轮停航了。

examples.en: Their savings weathered the recession better than expected.
examples.cn: 他们的储蓄比预期更好地挺过了衰退。

examples.en: Leave the planks outdoors to weather before you oil them.
examples.cn: 上油之前先把木板放在户外陈化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂（wea）— 遮（ther）」——天要变，先给自己遮一遮 → 天气；扛过去 → 经受住

root: 古英语 weder「空气、天空、风暴」，日耳曼诸语共有；其日耳曼语之前的来源不明，不作臆测。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the sky itself to the act of surviving it: first the state, then the storm, then endurance, then the slow damage exposure causes, and at last a reputation that stays afloat.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从天空本身走到「承受天空」这一动作：先是状态，再是风暴，再是承受，再是暴露造成的缓慢损伤，最后是仍浮着的声誉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flag on a mast taking whatever the sky sends, and still standing.
core.cn: 核心意象：桅杆上的旗承受天空送来的一切，却仍立着。

branches.en: THE SKY ITSELF: a neutral state that can turn hostile without changing its name.
branches.cn: 天空本身：中性的状态可以在不改名的情况下转为敌意。

branches.en: ENDURE: the ship that stays afloat is first a hull, then a reputation.
branches.cn: 承受：仍浮着的先是船体，后来是声誉。

branches.en: OPEN AIR AT WORK: the same exposure either damages or deliberately seasons.
branches.cn: 露天的作用：同一种暴露，或造成损伤，或被有意用于陈化。

branches.en: WINDWARD: the side that meets the weather first gives the noun a physical position.
branches.cn: 上风侧：最先迎受天气的一侧，使名词有了实体的方位。

branches.en: BELOW DECKS: seasickness became a mild everyday phrase for feeling unwell.
branches.cn: 甲板之下：晕船变成了日常说身体不适的轻微说法。

intro.en: Weather is a native Germanic word with native suffixes and compounds, so each part is English rather than Latin.
intro.cn: weather 是日耳曼语本族词，配本族后缀与复合成分，各部分属英语而非拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate of weder is known, so latinEntries is left empty instead of carrying a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: weder 没有已知可靠的拉丁同族词，因此 latinEntries 留空，不填重构形式。

items.example: The weather broke at dawn.
A weatherly hull can hold the wind.
The weathered paint flaked away.
items.exampleCN: 风化的漆皮一片片剥落。

items.example: A weatherproof jacket keeps the rain out.
items.exampleCN: 防风雨的外套能挡住雨。

items.example: The weatherman promised a dry weekend.
items.exampleCN: 气象播报员说周末无雨。

items.meaning: the process of decay by exposure
items.example: Weathering roughened the carved stone.

items.meaningCN: 因暴露而磨损或陈化的
items.example: Weathered oak needs no stain.
A weather-beaten hut stood on the point.
items.exampleCN: 岬角上立着一间饱经风雨的小屋。

items.example: They weatherized the roof seams.
items.exampleCN: 他们给屋顶接缝做了耐候处理。

definition_zh: 星期；周；一周（工作周）；七天的期间
definition_en: a period of seven days, usually counted from Monday to Sunday, and also the working days in it
core_image: 墙上挂历被撕下七页，边缘参差，露出新的一周
scene: 宿舍墙上挂着一本薄薄的日历，每过一天撕一页，撕下七页就在下面写一行小结。She tore off a page a day, and every week ended with a line of notes.
sceneCN: 这里 week 是「星期」（第 1 个义项：七天的期间）；句意为她每天撕一页，每周结束时写一行小结。被撕下七页、边缘参差的挂历就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 星期；周；工作周；一周的期间

senses.title: Seven days
senses.definition: a period of seven days, counted from a fixed day or from any day
senses.definitionCN: 从固定一日或任意一日算起的七天
senses.example: The course lasts six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课持续六个星期。
senses.why: This is the basic unit: a run of seven days.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本单位：连续七天。

senses.title: A calendar week
senses.definition: the seven days from Monday to Sunday as marked on a calendar
senses.definitionCN: 日历上从周一到周日的七天
senses.example: The report is due by the end of the week.
senses.exampleCN: 报告在本周末前到期。
senses.why: For schedules people count from Monday, giving the week a fixed frame.
senses.whyCN: 在日程安排中人们从周一数起，给一周一个固定框架。

senses.title: The working week
senses.definition: the days set aside for work, usually Monday to Friday
senses.definitionCN: 用于工作的那些日子，通常为周一到周五
senses.example: She works a four-day week.
senses.exampleCN: 她一周工作四天。
senses.why: From the seven days the word narrows to the days that count as work.
senses.whyCN: 从七天缩窄到算作工作的那些天。

senses.title: The week as a business period
senses.definition: the period a business or paper treats as one unit
senses.definitionCN: 商家或报刊所算作一个单位的期间
senses.example: This week we have three new offers.
senses.exampleCN: 本周我们有三项新的优惠。
senses.why: Traders cut the continuous cycle into weeks for counting sales and notices.
senses.whyCN: 商家把连续的循环切成周，用来计算销量与公告。

senses.title: Weak in compounds
senses.definition: used in compounds such as weekday, weekend and midweek to place events
senses.definitionCN: 用于 weekday、weekend、midweek 等复合词，标定时间位置
senses.example: Plans change at weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 周末的时候计划会变。
senses.why: Compounds let one word locate any event within the cycle.
senses.whyCN: 复合词让一个词把事情放到循环中的某处。

intro.en: Week is a Germanic word for a period of seven days, replacing an older English word of the same meaning.
intro.cn: week 是日耳曼语中表示七天的词，取代了同义的古英语旧词。

items.en: The Germanic root meant a turn or a series, and was applied to the cycle of days.
items.cn: 这一日耳曼词根意为一轮或一系列，被用来指日子的循环。

items.en: Wice named a week, while the older seofonnihte, seven nights, still served in law.
items.cn: wice 指一周，而更古老的 seofonnihte（七夜）在法律中仍在使用。

items.en: Week replaced the older counting form and became the ordinary word.
items.cn: week 取代了旧的计法，成为普通用词。

items.en: Compounds such as weekday and weekend fixed the week’s inner shape.
items.cn: weekday、weekend 等复合词固定了一周内部的形状。

items.en: A four-day week and a working week show the word measuring labour.
items.cn: a four-day week 与 working week 显示这个词可以衡量劳动。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like week, the second names neighbouring spans of time.
note.cn: 第一组与 week 形近音近，第二组是相邻的时间段。

entries.definition: Happening once every week.
Any day from Monday to Friday.
Saturday and Sunday.
Not strong, the same sound but different sense.
Two weeks, fourteen nights.
A period of about thirty days.
A fixed period of study or office.
Any length of time marked off.

normalIntro.en: Keep week as seven days first, then let compounds split it into work and rest.
normalIntro.cn: 先记住 week 是七天，再由复合词把它分成劳作与休息。

normal.en: Week is the span; weekday and weekend divide it.
normal.cn: week 是整段，weekday 与 weekend 把它分开。

normal.en: Weekly is the adjective and adverb.
normal.cn: weekly 是形容词也是副词。

normal.en: Do not confuse week with weak.
normal.cn: 不要把它与 weak 混淆。

normal.en: Within a week means before seven days pass.
normal.cn: within a week 意为七天之内。

normal.en: Week by week describes slow, steady change.
normal.cn: week by week 描述缓慢而稳定的变化。

abstract.en: Picture seven torn pages lying in a heap.
abstract.cn: 想七张撕下的纸堆在一起。

abstract.en: Feel the corner of the pad curl as you tear.
abstract.cn: 感受撕页时纸本边角卷起。

abstract.en: See a fresh page appear above the notes.
abstract.cn: 看笔记上方又出现一张新纸。

examples.en: We stayed in the mountains for a week.
examples.cn: 我们在山里待了一个星期。

examples.en: The shop opens late twice a week.
examples.cn: 这家店每周有两次开得晚。

examples.en: She has a busy week ahead of her.
examples.cn: 她接下来一周很忙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威克」——威克家的挂历一撕七页，就是一周，撕完一圈再从头。

root: 日耳曼语词根（一轮、一系列）→ 古英语 wice（一周）→ 中古英语 week；同源词有 weekday、weekend、weekly。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as seven days, narrows to the calendar frame and the working week, then works inside compounds.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从七天出发，缩窄到日历框架与工作周，再在复合词里发挥作用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: seven torn calendar pages.
core.cn: 核心意象：七张撕下的日历页。

branches.en: The span branch: a course lasting six weeks.
branches.cn: 长度分支：持续六周的课程。

branches.en: The calendar branch: due by the end of the week.
branches.cn: 日历分支：周末前到期。

branches.en: The work branch: a four-day week and a week of offers.
branches.cn: 工作分支：四天工作周与一周的优惠。

branches.en: The compound branch: plans that change at weekends.
branches.cn: 复合分支：周末变化的计划。

branches.en: The origin branch: a turn of the days.
branches.cn: 起源分支：日子的一轮。

intro.en: Week compounds with day, end and mid to place events, and takes -ly as an adjective and adverb.
intro.cn: week 与 day、end、mid 复合以标定时间，并加 -ly 作形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 称…的重量；重达；权衡；使烦恼
definition_en: to measure how heavy something is, to have a stated weight, and to think carefully about choices
core_image: 老式天平两端各放一只盘，指针在刻度间来回摆动最后停住
scene: 集市上卖水果的老板把袋子放上秤盘，指针一晃，最后停在一个数上，他报出价来。The seller put the bag on the scale to weigh it and waited for the needle to settle.
sceneCN: 这里 weigh 是「称重」（第 1 个义项：测量某物有多重）；句意为摊主把袋子放上秤，等指针停稳。两端摆动的天平与指针就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 称…的重量；重达；权衡；使忧心

senses.title: To measure weight
senses.definition: to find out how heavy something is, using a scale
senses.definitionCN: 用秤查明某物有多重
senses.example: The nurse weighed the baby at every visit.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每次来访都给婴儿称重。
senses.why: This is the core sense: the balance answers a question of heaviness.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义：天平回答「有多重」的问题。

senses.title: To have a stated weight
senses.definition: to be of a particular heaviness
senses.definitionCN: 具有某个特定的重量
senses.example: This parcel weighs almost two kilos.
senses.exampleCN: 这个包裹重近两公斤。
senses.why: The verb takes the weight as its own measure, so no object is needed.
senses.whyCN: 动词自身带上重量，因此不需要宾语。

senses.title: To think about choices
senses.definition: to compare facts or options carefully before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在决定前仔细比较事实或选项
senses.example: The committee weighed the risks before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在投票前权衡了风险。
senses.why: A balance holds two pans, and a mind holds two options the same way.
senses.whyCN: 天平托着两只盘，头脑也同样托着两个选择。

senses.title: To be a burden on someone
senses.definition: to trouble or oppress a person’s mind
senses.definitionCN: 使某人心里烦恼、沉重
senses.example: The decision weighed on her for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定压在她心上好几周。
senses.why: Something heavy presses down, so worry is said to weigh on a mind.
senses.whyCN: 沉重的东西会向下压，于是忧虑被说成压在心头。

senses.title: To raise a ship’s anchor
senses.definition: of a ship, to lift the anchor before sailing
senses.definitionCN: 指船在启航前把锚拉起
senses.example: The fleet weighed anchor at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 船队在黎明起锚。
senses.why: A phrase from sailing, kept because anchor and balance share the idea of lifting.
senses.whyCN: 这是航海用语，因为起锚与天平共通「抬起」的意象而保留。

intro.en: Weigh comes from Old English wegan, to carry or to lift, the same root that gives wagon and the Latin vehere, to carry.
intro.cn: weigh 来自古英语 wegan（搬运、抬起），与 wagon 及拉丁语 vehere（运载）同根。

items.en: The root meant to move or carry a load, and weighing was done by lifting and comparing.
items.cn: 这一词根意为移动或承载，古时称量靠抬起并比较。

items.en: Wegan meant to carry, to lift and to weigh, all in one verb.
items.cn: wegan 一名兼指搬运、抬起与称量。

items.en: The spelling weigh appeared, and the past form became weighed under French-influenced habits.
items.cn: 拼写 weigh 出现，过去式在法语影响下成为 weighed。

items.en: The weighing of evidence extended the word to judgement and decision.
items.cn: 权衡证据把词义扩展到判断与决断。

items.en: Weight, the noun, came from the same root and now names the thing measured.
items.cn: 名词 weight 出自同根，如今指被测量的那份东西。

note.en: The first group shares the weigh root and shape, the second the words used in measuring and deciding.
note.cn: 第一组与 weigh 同根形近，第二组是测量与决断中的近义词。

normalIntro.en: Start with the balance, then let it tilt into decisions and into worry.
normalIntro.cn: 先看天平，再让它倾斜出去，成为决断与忧虑。

normal.en: Weigh is the verb; weight is the noun.
normal.cn: weigh 是动词，weight 是名词。

normal.en: Weigh about ten kilos needs no object.
normal.cn: weigh about ten kilos 不带宾语。

normal.en: Weigh the options means put each one on the balance.
normal.cn: weigh the options 就是把每个选择放上天平。

normal.en: Weigh on someone means press down on the mind.
normal.cn: weigh on someone 是压在某人心上。

normal.en: Weigh anchor is the opposite of drop anchor.
normal.cn: weigh anchor 与 drop anchor 相反。

abstract.en: Picture a needle swinging and dying away.
abstract.cn: 想指针摆动后慢慢停住。

abstract.en: Hear the small click of a brass weight set down.
abstract.cn: 听铜砝码落下时轻轻一响。

abstract.en: Feel one side sink and the other rise.
abstract.cn: 感受一头下沉、一头升起。

examples.en: Please weigh this parcel before you post it.
examples.cn: 寄之前请称一下这个包裹。

examples.en: She weighs less than she did last year.
examples.cn: 她比去年轻了些。

examples.en: You must weigh the cost against the benefit.
examples.cn: 你必须把成本与收益权衡一下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂」——摊主喊一声「喂」，把袋子往秤上一放，看指针停在哪。

root: 日耳曼语词根（搬运、抬举）→ 古英语 wegan（搬、抬、称）→ weigh；同根词有 weight、wagon，拉丁语 vehere。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts at the balance, states a weight, then moves to weighing options, to weighing on a mind, and to lifting an anchor.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从天平出发，报出重量，再转为权衡选择、压在心头，最后是起锚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale needle settling.
core.cn: 核心意象：停住的秤针。

branches.en: The measure branch: weighing a baby and weighing two kilos.
branches.cn: 测量分支：给婴儿称重与重两公斤。

branches.en: The judgement branch: comparing risks before a vote.
branches.cn: 判断分支：投票前比较风险。

branches.en: The burden branch: a decision that presses for weeks.
branches.cn: 负担分支：压了数周的决定。

branches.en: The sailing branch: anchor lifted at dawn.
branches.cn: 航海分支：黎明起锚。

branches.en: The scale and the mind share one image: two pans, then two choices.
branches.cn: 天平与头脑共用一个意象：两只盘，两个选择。

intro.en: Weigh takes regular endings and the noun weight from the same root.
intro.cn: weigh 用规则词尾，名词 weight 出自同一词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cousin vehere means to carry, and the table shows how the same image spread.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词 vehere 意为运载，拉丁表展示同一意象的扩散。
